k: Black Bolt's brother, born without powers
st: Maximus seizes Attilan in a coup and sends the royal family fleeing to Earth.
Black Bolt seals Maximus in a vault as Attilan is abandoned.

k: Head of Attilan's Royal Guard
st: Auran, who can heal from any wound, hunts the royals on Earth for Maximus. Auran comes back from a deadly blast and fights on for Maximus as the royals lead their people out of Attilan.

k: An Inhuman with destructive eyes
st: Mordis hunts the royal family on Earth and dies bringing a building down.

k: A scientist studying Inhumans
st: Declan works for Maximus and experiments on Black Bolt.
A revived, raging Gorgon throws Declan into a Terrigenesis chamber, killing him.

k: A group of wealthy Los Angeles parents
st: The parents of PRIDE secretly sacrifice teens for Jonah, until their own kids find out and run.
PRIDE join their children against the threats that come for their families.

k: A powerful man who funds PRIDE
st: Jonah needs PRIDE's sacrifices to live, and he kidnaps his daughter Karolina and others.
Nico stabs Jonah with the Staff of One, and he falls.
In a new body, Jonah traps Karolina and Chase, until Molly knocks him down and the Runaways trap him.

k: A sorceress from the Dark Dimension
st: Morgan le Fay lures Nico deeper into dark magic.
Tina's spell banishes Morgan back to the Dark Dimension.

k: A New Orleans police detective
st: Connors killed Tyrone's brother years ago and is still covering it up.
Tyrone absorbs Connors with his cloak and traps him in the Dark Dimension.
Back on Earth, Connors tries to make amends, until Tyrone's mother Adina shoots him dead.

k: A Roxxon executive
st: Scarborough tries to bury the truth about the Roxxon rig explosion that killed Tandy's father.
Tandy traps Scarborough in his own mind, leaving him in a coma.

k: A jazz musician with a dark gift
st: Andre runs a trafficking ring and feeds on people's despair to grow stronger.
Tandy and Tyrone defeat Andre in the finale.

k: Oscorp's founder, desperate to save his company
st: Norman Osborn tests a strength serum on himself, goes mad and kills his colleague Dr. Stromm. As the Green Goblin, he kills the Oscorp board at the World Unity Festival in Times Square. He learns Peter is Spider-Man and attacks Aunt May in her home. He drops Mary Jane and a tram full of children from the Queensboro Bridge to test Spider-Man.
His own glider impales him, and he begs Peter not to tell Harry.
Pulled across universes, the Goblin takes over Norman again and fatally wounds Aunt May.
The Spider-Men cure him at the Statue of Liberty, and he is sent home.

k: A thief who robs a wrestling promoter
st: He robs a wrestling promoter, and Peter lets him run past.
He shoots Uncle Ben and steals his car, then falls from a warehouse window to his death.
Police reveal Dennis Carradine was only the getaway man; Flint Marko fired the shot.

k: Otto Octavius, a gentle fusion scientist
st: Otto Octavius's fusion demo fails, killing his wife Rosie and fusing his AI arms to his spine. Driven by the arms, he robs a bank to rebuild his reactor and takes Aunt May hostage. To get Harry Osborn's tritium, he fights Spider-Man on a train and delivers him to Harry.
Peter talks him down, and Otto sinks his reactor in the river, drowning with it.
Pulled across universes, he fights Peter on a bridge until Stark nanotech takes over his arms.
With his inhibitor chip fixed, Otto helps cure the other villains at the Statue of Liberty.

k: Peter's best friend, Norman Osborn's son
st: Harry blames Spider-Man for his father's death and trades tritium to Doc Ock for Spider-Man. He unmasks Peter, then finds his father's hidden Goblin gear.
Harry attacks Peter on a glider, then loses his memory after a fall. His memory back, he forces Mary Jane to break up with Peter, and a pumpkin bomb scars his face.
Harry joins Peter to save Mary Jane and dies taking a glider blade meant for Peter.

k: Flint Marko, an escaped convict with a sick daughter
st: Escaped convict Flint Marko falls into a particle test and becomes living sand. He robs an armored car, and Peter washes him away in a subway tunnel. He teams with Venom to kill Spider-Man and holds Mary Jane hostage.
Marko admits he shot Uncle Ben by accident, Peter forgives him, and he drifts away.
Pulled across universes, he is locked in the Sanctum, desperate to get home to his daughter.
He fights the Spider-Men at the Statue of Liberty until they cure him.

k: Eddie Brock, a rival Daily Bugle photographer
st: Eddie Brock fakes a photo of Spider-Man committing a crime, and Peter gets him fired.
The alien symbiote Peter tore off bonds with Eddie, creating Venom. Venom teams with the Sandman and kidnaps Mary Jane to lure Spider-Man.
Peter rips Eddie free with sound, and Eddie dies leaping after the symbiote into a pumpkin bomb.

k: Dr. Curt Connors, a one-armed Oscorp scientist
st: Under Oscorp pressure, Dr. Curt Connors tests his lizard serum on himself to regrow his arm. As the Lizard, he attacks the Williamsburg Bridge, and Spider-Man saves a boy from a falling car. He tries to turn New York into lizards with a gas device on Oscorp Tower and kills Captain Stacy.
Spider-Man releases the antidote, and Connors returns to human form and is jailed.
Pulled across universes as the Lizard, he ends up in the Sanctum's cells.
He fights the Spider-Men at the Statue of Liberty until they cure him.

k: A mysterious man in the shadows
st: A man in the shadows visits Connors in his cell and asks about Peter's father.
He meets Harry at Ravencroft and agrees to start building a team. He frees Aleksei Sytsevich and gives him a rhino battle suit.

k: Max Dillon, a lonely Oscorp electrician
st: Oscorp electrician Max Dillon falls into a tank of electric eels and becomes living electricity.
He wrecks Times Square, Spider-Man shorts him out, and he is locked in Ravencroft.
Harry Osborn frees him, and Electro blacks out the city from a power station.
Spider-Man and Gwen overload him, and he explodes.
Pulled across universes, Max ends up in the Sanctum and wants to keep his power.
He powers up at the Statue of Liberty until Otto helps the Spider-Men cure him.

k: Peter's childhood friend, new head of Oscorp
st: Dying of his father's inherited disease, Harry demands Spider-Man's blood, and Peter refuses.
Ousted from Oscorp, he frees Electro from Ravencroft to break into the company. Harry injects the spider venom, dons Oscorp armor and becomes the Green Goblin.
Gwen Stacy dies in his clock tower fight with Spider-Man, and Harry is locked in Ravencroft. From his cell, he tells the Gentleman to start forming a team.

k: Aleksei Sytsevich, a Russian mobster
st: Aleksei Sytsevich hijacks an Oscorp plutonium truck, and Spider-Man has him arrested.
Freed in a rhino battle suit, he tears through the streets and calls Spider-Man out.

k: An ambitious Oscorp executive
st: Donald Menken frames Harry for a cover-up and takes control of Oscorp.

k: A cruel doctor at Ravencroft
st: Dr. Kafka runs painful experiments on the captive Max Dillon at Ravencroft.

k: Eddie Brock, a disgraced reporter
st: Reporter Eddie Brock bonds with an alien symbiote while exposing the Life Foundation. Venom destroys Riot's rocket and vows to eat only bad guys.
Eddie and Venom split, then reunite to stop Carnage at a cathedral.
Pulled into a new universe, Eddie learns about Spider-Man and the Avengers at a bar. Doctor Strange's spell sends him home, leaving a piece of the symbiote behind.
Hunted by Knull's creatures and the army, the symbiote dies saving Eddie at Area 55.

k: An alien symbiote, leader of its kind
st: Riot escapes a crash in Malaysia and jumps between hosts toward the Life Foundation.
Bonded to Carlton Drake, Riot burns up when Venom blows up the rocket.

k: The Life Foundation's billionaire founder
st: Carlton Drake tests alien symbiotes on homeless people at the Life Foundation.
He bonds with Riot and tries to launch a rocket to bring more symbiotes to Earth.
Venom wrecks the rocket, and Drake dies in the explosion.

k: Carlton Drake's head of security
st: Roland Treece hunts Eddie for Drake until Venom kills him.

k: A serial killer on death row
st: Serial killer Cletus Kasady tells Eddie from his San Quentin cell there will be carnage.
Kasady bites Eddie, and a symbiote spawn turns him into Carnage at his execution. Carnage frees Frances Barrison from Ravencroft and goes on a killing spree.
At the cathedral, Venom devours the Carnage symbiote and Kasady.

k: Frances Barrison, a woman with a sonic scream
st: Young Frances Barrison is torn from Cletus Kasady and locked away for her sonic scream.
Carnage frees her from Ravencroft, and the two plan to wed at a cathedral.
She dies in the cathedral battle.

k: The creator of the symbiotes, imprisoned
st: From his prison, Knull sends Xenophages to Earth to take the Codex from Eddie and Venom.

k: Knull's symbiote-hunting beasts
st: Knull's hunters track Eddie and Venom across the country for the Codex.
At Area 55 the symbiotes fight them, and Venom destroys them at the cost of its life.

k: A general who hunts symbiotes
st: General Rex Strickland's soldiers hunt Eddie and Venom, then face the Xenophages at Area 55.

k: Dr. Michael Morbius, a dying genius
st: Seeking a cure, Dr. Michael Morbius uses vampire bat DNA and kills the mercenaries on his ship. Blamed for killings, he hunts the real killer, his friend Milo. After defeating Milo, Michael flees with a swarm of bats.

k: Lucien, Michael's lifelong friend
st: Milo steals the bat serum and becomes a killer vampire. He kills Dr. Nicholas and attacks Martine to provoke Michael.
Michael injects him with antibodies that kill him.

k: A man who stole the power of a spider
st: In the Amazon in 1973, Ezekiel Sims kills Constance Webb to steal a rare spider. Haunted by visions of three girls killing him, he hunts them in 2003 with stolen NSA tools.
Cassie Webb leads him into a trap, and he dies in the final fight.

k: Ezekiel Sims's tech expert
st: Amaria uses stolen NSA tools to track the three girls for Ezekiel Sims.

k: Sergei Kravinoff, a crime lord's son
st: Saved by a potion after a lion attack, Sergei Kravinoff gains animal strength and hunts criminals. He lures a bear to kill his father, Nikolai, and embraces life as Kraven the Hunter.

k: A ruthless Russian crime lord
st: Nikolai Kravinoff rules his sons with cruelty and leaves Sergei for dead after a lion attack.
Sergei learns Nikolai used his sons against Aleksei Sytsevich and lures a bear that kills him.

k: Aleksei Sytsevich, a crime boss
st: Aleksei Sytsevich, a mobster with serum-hardened skin, kidnaps Dmitri to draw out Kraven.
He transforms into the Rhino in the final battle, and Kraven kills him.

k: An assassin who can hypnotize
st: The Foreigner, an assassin hired by Sytsevich, hunts Kraven with hypnotic tricks.
He drugs Kraven with a neurotoxin, but Calypso kills him with a crossbow.

k: Kraven's younger brother, a gifted mimic
st: Dmitri, a timid mimic of any voice, is kidnapped to lure his brother Sergei. Remade by the doctor behind the Rhino, he takes over his father's empire as the Chameleon.

k: Wilson Fisk, a towering crime lord
st: Wilson Fisk builds a super collider to reach other universes and find his late wife and son. He kills his universe's Peter Parker in front of Miles. He shoots the Prowler for sparing Miles.
Miles stuns him, wrecks the collider and leaves him webbed up for the police.

k: Kingpin's silent masked enforcer
st: The Prowler hunts Miles for Kingpin across Brooklyn.
Revealed as Miles's uncle Aaron Davis, he refuses to kill Miles, and Kingpin shoots him dead.

k: Dr. Olivia Octavius, Kingpin's head scientist
st: Dr. Olivia Octavius runs Kingpin's collider and chases Miles and Peter B. Parker across Alchemax.
In the final fight at the collider, a vehicle pulled through the vortex plows into her.

k: One of Kingpin's heavies
st: Tombstone attacks the Spider-People for Kingpin, and Jefferson Davis puts him in a patrol car.

k: Kingpin's stinger-tailed enforcer
st: Scorpion attacks the Spider-People at Aunt May's house, and Spider-Ham beats him at the collider.

k: A hulking monster working for Kingpin
st: The Green Goblin fights Spider-Man at Kingpin's collider and dies in the blast.

k: Dr. Jonathan Ohnn, covered in portals
st: Dr. Jonathan Ohnn, scarred by the collider, robs an ATM as the Spot and blames Miles for his life. He jumps to Mumbattan to raid its Alchemax, causing a disaster. He dives into a collider, gains vast power and threatens Miles's world.

k: A Renaissance-style Vulture from another universe
st: Pulled into Gwen's world, the Vulture attacks the Guggenheim Museum.
Gwen, Jessica Drew and Spider-Man 2099 capture him and send him home.

k: Spider-Man 2099, leader of the Spider Society
st: Miguel O'Hara orders the Spider Society to stop Miles from saving his father.

k: A Miles Morales from Earth-42
st: On Earth-42, Miles G. Morales is the Prowler, and he captures the Miles from Earth-1610.

k: A ghoulish villain who dabbles in witchcraft
st: The Green Goblin hypnotizes J. Jonah Jameson to summon demons from the spirit world.
Spider-Man tips over his cauldron in a cemetery and webs him up.
Dr. Noah Boddy breaks him out of prison, but Spider-Man tricks the villains into fighting each other and webs them for the police.

k: A scientist with four metal arms
st: Doctor Octopus plots to cut the city's utilities and traps Spider-Man and Betty Brant in his cave.
Spider-Man blinds him with webbing, and police called by Betty arrest him.

k: Dr. Connors, a scientist in the Florida swamps
st: Testing a swamp fever serum on himself, Dr. Connors becomes the Lizard and terrorizes the Everglades.
Spider-Man makes him drink an antidote at an old Spanish fort, and he returns to his family.

k: A winged thief
st: The Vulture turns flocks of birds on New York for a ransom, but Spider-Man turns the birds on him and he flees.
Dr. Noah Boddy breaks him out of prison, but Spider-Man tricks the villains into fighting each other and webs them for the police.

k: A criminal who controls electricity
st: Electro uses his powers for crime until Spider-Man traps him in special webbing and hands him over.
A storm recharges Electro, who escapes jail and seizes the city's power station until Spider-Man nets him again.
Dr. Noah Boddy breaks him out of prison, but Spider-Man tricks the villains into fighting each other and webs them for the police.

k: A master of illusions
st: Mysterio frames Spider-Man for a robbery and offers to trap him for J. Jonah Jameson.
Spider-Man records Mysterio confessing, beats him and leaves him for the police.

k: A man mutated into a human scorpion
st: Created by Dr. Stillwell for one of J. Jonah Jameson's schemes, the Scorpion turns on Jameson.
Spider-Man webs him up for the police, then catches him again after he escapes prison.

k: A criminal made of sand
st: The Sandman steals the Goliath Diamond, frames Spider-Man and demands a ransom.
Spider-Man knocks him into a vat of water, and the soggy Sandman is handed to the police.

k: Wilson Fisk, a respected philanthropist
st: Wilson Fisk poses as a philanthropist while secretly running New York's underworld.
He backs the Insidious Six and the Spider-Slayers in plots to destroy Spider-Man.
He reunites the Insidious Six and tries to activate the Red Skull's doomsday device.

k: Otto Octavius, a brilliant scientist
st: A lab accident fuses Otto Octavius to his mechanical arms.
He leads the Insidious Six against Spider-Man.

k: A masked mercenary on a glider
st: The Hobgoblin plays Norman Osborn and the Kingpin against each other for profit.
He returns to work with the Kingpin, until he is unmasked as Jason Macendale and arrested.

k: Norman Osborn, Oscorp's ruthless owner
st: Norman Osborn becomes the Green Goblin and attacks Spider-Man.
Pushed into a breakdown, Norman becomes the Green Goblin again and battles the Hobgoblin.
He kidnaps Mary Jane, and both vanish through a dimensional portal.

k: Norman Osborn's son, out for revenge
st: Harry Osborn follows his father's footsteps and becomes the new Green Goblin to kill Spider-Man.
As the Green Goblin again, he attacks Peter and Mary Jane's wedding and is defeated.

k: Eddie Brock, a disgraced reporter
st: The alien symbiote Peter rejects bonds with reporter Eddie Brock, creating Venom.
The roar of a rocket launch tears the symbiote off Eddie, and Spider-Man sends it into space.
Baron Mordo and Dormammu restore his symbiote, but Venom refuses to keep serving them.
Venom sacrifices himself, vanishing into a portal with Carnage to save Dr. Ashley Kafka.

k: Cletus Kasady, Eddie Brock's cellmate
st: With help from Baron Mordo and Dormammu, Cletus Kasady bonds with a symbiote and becomes Carnage.
Carnage steals life energy for Dormammu until a reversed portal pulls him in, along with Venom.

k: A sorcerer who serves Dormammu
st: Baron Mordo's cult kidnaps Mary Jane and uses the Wand of Watoomb to open a portal to the Dark Dimension.
Spider-Man, Doctor Strange and Wong defeat him and take back the wand.
He restores Eddie Brock's symbiote and helps create Carnage to feed Dormammu.

k: A demon lord of the Dark Dimension
st: Dormammu has Baron Mordo open a portal so he can enter Earth's dimension.
He has Carnage steal life energy for him, until Venom and Carnage fall through his portal.

k: The genius son of Spencer Smythe
st: Alistair Smythe builds Spider-Slayers for the Kingpin, blaming Spider-Man for his father's loss.
He becomes a cyborg, the Ultimate Spider-Slayer.

k: Mac Gargan, a private eye
st: Private eye Mac Gargan is turned into the Scorpion by an experiment J. Jonah Jameson paid for.
He joins the Insidious Six against Spider-Man.

k: Dr. Curt Connors, a reptile researcher
st: Dr. Curt Connors becomes the Lizard and hides in the sewers until Spider-Man cures him.

k: Quentin Beck, a special effects wizard
st: Quentin Beck frames Spider-Man for crimes using special effects until Spider-Man exposes him.
He joins the Insidious Six against Spider-Man.

k: A thief with vibration gauntlets
st: The Shocker blasts Spider-Man with vibration gauntlets and joins the Insidious Six.

k: Adrian Toomes, an aging inventor
st: Adrian Toomes, an aging winged inventor, tries to drain Spider-Man's youth to become young again.

k: A thug in a rhino suit
st: The Rhino charges Spider-Man in his armored suit and joins the Insidious Six.

k: A master of disguise
st: The Chameleon uses his disguises against Spider-Man as part of the Insidious Six.

k: Sergei Kravinoff, a big-game hunter
st: Kraven, given animal powers by a serum, hunts Spider-Man.
He gives up the hunt and leaves to start a new life.

k: Michael Morbius, a college student
st: An experiment turns student Michael Morbius into a vampire who craves plasma.

k: Morrie Bench, Mary Jane's ex-boyfriend
st: Morrie Bench becomes Hydro-Man and goes after Mary Jane, his ex-girlfriend.
Mary Jane leads him away from water, and he evaporates.
A clone of Hydro-Man made by Miles Warren returns and kidnaps Mary Jane.

k: An aging crime boss
st: Silvermane uses an ancient tablet to restore his youth, but grows younger until he is a baby.

k: A flat-headed mob enforcer
st: Hammerhead does Silvermane's dirty work and fights Spider-Man.

k: A mob enforcer from Robbie Robertson's past
st: Tombstone, a childhood friend of Robbie Robertson, pulls him into crime.

k: A Peter Parker bonded to Carnage
st: A Peter Parker from another universe, bonded to Carnage, tries to destroy all realities.
His own world's Uncle Ben reaches him, and he sacrifices himself.

k: Ruler of Counter-Earth
st: On Counter-Earth, the High Evolutionary rules humans through his animal-human Bestials.

k: A tiger warrior, Knight of Wundagore
st: Lord Tyger serves the High Evolutionary as one of the Knights of Wundagore.

k: Knight of Wundagore, a ram warrior
st: Sir Ram serves the High Evolutionary as a Knight of Wundagore and hires an assassin to kill Spider-Man.

k: Eddie Brock, bonded to the symbiote
st: Venom and Carnage hijack John Jameson's ship bound for Counter-Earth, and it crashes there. Working for the Synoptic, Venom plots with the High Evolutionary to unleash millions of symbiotes.

k: Cletus Kasady, bonded to a red symbiote
st: Carnage and Venom hijack John Jameson's ship bound for Counter-Earth, and it crashes there. Working for the Synoptic, Carnage plots with the High Evolutionary to unleash millions of symbiotes.

k: Adrian Toomes, an inventor with a grudge
st: Adrian Toomes attacks Norman Osborn for stealing his flight tech, and Spider-Man stops him.
Freed by Doctor Octopus, he joins the Sinister Six, and Spider-Man beats the team.
He returns in the re-formed Sinister Six at Christmas, then vanishes from police custody.

k: Max Dillon, a lab assistant
st: A lab accident turns Max Dillon into living electricity.
Freed by Doctor Octopus, he joins the Sinister Six, and Spider-Man beats the team.
He returns in the re-formed Sinister Six at Christmas, then vanishes from police custody.
Spider-Man captures him at the Master Planner's hidden lair.

k: Dr. Curt Connors, Peter's science mentor
st: Dr. Curt Connors tests a reptile serum on himself and becomes the Lizard.
Spider-Man cures him with an antidote.

k: Montana, Ox and Fancy Dan, hired muscle
st: The Big Man's hired thugs Montana, Ox and Fancy Dan try to take out Spider-Man and fail.
Fancy Dan returns as Ricochet, and he and Ox join the Shocker as the new Enforcers until Spider-Man beats them.

k: Montana, leader of the Enforcers
st: Montana takes a vibration suit from the Tinkerer and attacks Spider-Man as the Shocker.
Freed by Doctor Octopus, he joins the Sinister Six, and Spider-Man beats the team.

k: Flint Marko, a small-time crook
st: Crook Flint Marko gains a body of sand and fights Spider-Man for the Big Man.
Freed by Doctor Octopus, he joins the Sinister Six, and Spider-Man beats the team.
He returns in the re-formed Sinister Six at Christmas, then vanishes from police custody.
He saves an oil tanker crew and seems to die in the blast, but he slips away intact.

k: Alex O'Hirn, a thug in a bonded rhino suit
st: Thug Alex O'Hirn is bonded to an armored rhino suit and charges Spider-Man.
Freed by Doctor Octopus, he joins the Sinister Six, and Spider-Man beats the team.
He returns in the re-formed Sinister Six at Christmas, and Spider-Man beats him again.

k: Tombstone, a hidden crime lord
st: L. Thompson Lincoln, the crime lord called Tombstone, secretly creates super villains to run New York.
His Valentine's Day summit erupts into a gang war, and he is arrested but soon makes bail.

k: A masked master of illusions
st: Mysterio attacks Spider-Man, but the man Spider-Man unmasks and hands to police is a robot decoy.
He joins the re-formed Sinister Six at Christmas, and Spider-Man catches him.

k: Otto Octavius, a timid scientist
st: A lab accident fuses timid scientist Otto Octavius to his mechanical harness.
He breaks out villains to form the Sinister Six against Spider-Man, and he is jailed.
Unmasked as the Master Planner at his hidden lair, he escapes in a pod.
He joins a Valentine's Day gang war until Spider-Man subdues him, and he is arrested.

k: A masked madman on a glider
st: The Green Goblin plays the crime bosses against each other and torments Spider-Man.
He secretly sparks a gang war between Tombstone, Silvermane and Doctor Octopus, then takes over the underworld.
Revealed as Norman Osborn, who framed his own son Harry, he fakes his death and slips away in disguise.

k: Eddie Brock, Peter's old friend
st: Eddie Brock bonds with the alien symbiote Peter rejected and becomes Venom.
Spider-Man tricks the symbiote off Eddie and traps it in wet cement, and Eddie drops out of sight.
Venom returns, but Spider-Man strips the symbiote off with a gene cleanser, and Eddie is sent to Ravencroft.

k: A master of disguise
st: The Chameleon impersonates Spider-Man to frame him for crimes.
Norman Osborn uses the Chameleon's disguises to throw Spider-Man off the Goblin's trail.

k: Sergei Kravinoff, a famous hunter
st: Kraven the Hunter comes to New York to make Spider-Man his prey.
He joins the re-formed Sinister Six at Christmas, then vanishes from police custody.

k: Mark Allan, Liz Allan's brother
st: Mark Allan gains a molten body and fights Spider-Man as the Molten Man.

k: Phineas Mason, a gadget maker
st: Phineas Mason builds weapons and suits for the Big Man's villains.

k: A flat-headed mob enforcer
st: Hammerhead enforces for New York's crime bosses and fights Spider-Man.
Secretly played by the Goblin, he betrays Tombstone at a Valentine's Day summit and sparks a gang war.

k: An old-school crime boss
st: Silvermane battles the other crime bosses for control of New York.
At a Valentine's Day summit he fights in hydraulic armor until Spider-Man disables it and police take him.

k: A ruthless 1930s mob boss
st: Silvermane rules the 1930s New York underworld as Ben Reilly digs into his empire.
Cat Hardy turns on Silvermane and shoots him dead.

k: Flint Marko, Silvermane's muscle
st: Flint Marko, given powers by wartime experiments, does Silvermane's dirty work.
Ben gives him the last dose of the cure, so he can be with Cat Hardy.

k: Lonnie Lincoln, Silvermane's enforcer
st: Lonnie Lincoln serves as one of Silvermane's powered enforcers.
Robbie Robertson injects him with the cure, and he slips past police to leave town with his mother.

k: An electric enforcer for Silvermane
st: Megawatt, given electric powers by wartime experiments, works as one of Silvermane's goons.
Ben beats him in a showdown on a train, and Megawatt dies.

k: A scientist who stole from Oscorp
st: Otto Octavius secretly arms criminals with advanced tech, turning them into super villains. He gives Mila Masaryk a laser helmet, creating the Unicorn.
Police arrest him for breaking the Sokovia Accords, and his tech is seized. Norman Osborn gloats over a deal with Secretary Ross for Otto's inventions, and Otto vows to get him.

k: Leader of the Scorpions gang
st: Mac Gargan's Scorpions gang wars with Big Donovan's 110th Street Gang. In Otto's suit he becomes the Scorpion and badly hurts Spider-Man. In a gang war, Spider-Man beats him savagely until Lonnie stops the killing blow.

k: Boss of the 110th Street Gang
st: Big Donovan takes Lonnie into his gang and names him Tombstone after Lonnie saves him. When Gargan nearly kills him, he flees and leaves Lonnie behind.

k: A high school football star
st: To protect his brother, Lonnie Lincoln joins the 110th Street Gang. After he saves Big Donovan, the gang starts calling him Tombstone. Drenched in DIOX-3 gas, he gains rock-hard skin and stays to rebuild the gang after Big Donovan flees.

k: Mila Masaryk, a criminal
st: Mila Masaryk escapes a robbery bust, then breaks her crew out of prison with Otto's laser helmet as the Unicorn.
She uses her partner Mikhail as bait, and after he takes her helmet, police arrest her.

k: A member of a robbery crew
st: Dmitri Smerdyakov is jailed after a robbery, and the Unicorn breaks him out.

k: A member of a robbery crew
st: Mikhail Sytsevich is jailed after a robbery, and the Unicorn breaks him out.
When Spider-Man saves him, Mikhail takes the Unicorn's helmet to spare Spider-Man, and police arrest him.

k: A petty crook with super-speed boots
st: James Sanders, a crook with super-speed gear, teams with Tarantula until Spider-Man, coached by Norman, takes them down.

k: A crook with energy blade gauntlets
st: Maria Vasquez, a crook with blade gauntlets, teams with Speed Demon until Spider-Man, coached by Norman, takes them down.

k: A horned brute in an armored hide
st: The Rhino rams a train to steal the first part of a top secret military weapon.
Spider-Man traps him in baked mud at his zoo hideout, and the police take him in.

k: A scientist who makes himself invisible
st: Made invisible by his own machine, Dr. Noah Boddy seeks revenge on J. Jonah Jameson for mocking his theory.
He frees the Vulture, Electro and the Green Goblin, but Spider-Man turns them on each other and leaves all four for the police.

k: An electric enforcer on Counter-Earth
st: Spider-Man breaks into the High Evolutionary's tower and runs into Electro.

k: A mutant master of magnetism who distrusts humanity
st: Magneto kidnaps Senator Kelly and tests a machine that forces humans to mutate.
He aims the machine at world leaders on Ellis Island, but the X-Men stop him and he lands in a plastic prison.
Freed by Mystique, he joins the X-Men against Stryker, then turns Cerebro against humanity.
He builds a new Brotherhood, recruits the Phoenix, and attacks Alcatraz to destroy the mutant cure. Beast injects him with the cure, but alone in a park he makes a metal chess piece move.
In a mid-credits scene, Magneto, his powers restored, meets Logan at an airport to warn him of a new threat to mutants.
In a dark future, he fights the Sentinels side by side with Charles Xavier.

k: A shape-shifting mutant who serves Magneto
st: Mystique poses as Bobby Drake to sabotage Cerebro, then fights the X-Men at the Statue of Liberty. Wolverine stabs her, but she survives and takes Senator Kelly's place in public.
She breaks Magneto out of his plastic prison and helps the X-Men raid Stryker's base.
Freed from a prison convoy, she takes a cure dart meant for Magneto and loses her powers.
Abandoned by Magneto, she tells the government where to find him.

k: A feral mutant enforcer in Magneto's Brotherhood
st: Sabretooth ambushes Wolverine and Rogue on a snowy road, then captures Rogue for Magneto.
Cyclops blasts him out of the Statue of Liberty's head, and he falls far below.
In the Void, a Sabretooth variant takes on Wolverine, and Wolverine cuts off his head.

k: A leaping, long-tongued mutant in the Brotherhood
st: Toad fights the X-Men at the train station and inside the Statue of Liberty.
Storm strikes him with lightning, and he falls into the water.
A Toad variant fights for Cassandra Nova in the Void, and Blade kills him in the raid on her lair.

k: John Allerdyce, a hot-headed student who controls fire
st: John Allerdyce sets police cars ablaze, then leaves the X-Men to join Magneto at Alkali Lake.
As Pyro, he joins the Brotherhood's attack on Alcatraz, and Iceman beats him in a duel.
In the Void, he serves Cassandra Nova while secretly working for Paradox of the TVA.
Cassandra Nova learns of his betrayal and kills him.

k: A U.S. Army officer running secret mutant programs
st: Stryker leads Team X, a covert unit of mutant soldiers, on brutal missions. He bonds adamantium to Logan's skeleton in the Weapon X program, then orders his memory wiped. He unleashes Weapon XI, then shoots Logan in the head with adamantium bullets, erasing his memory.
Military police arrest him for the murder of General Munson.
Stryker raids the X-Mansion and uses his son's power to turn Cerebro against every mutant.
Wolverine leaves him chained at Alkali Lake, and he dies when the dam bursts.

k: Yuriko, Stryker's mind-controlled mutant bodyguard
st: Under Stryker's control, Yuriko serves as his silent enforcer at Alkali Lake.
Wolverine floods her body with liquid adamantium, and she dies.
A Lady Deathstrike variant stands among Cassandra Nova's forces in the Void.

k: Stryker's son, a mutant who casts illusions
st: Stryker uses Jason's illusions to control Charles Xavier through a copy of Cerebro.
Storm and Nightcrawler free Xavier, and Jason is left behind as the base floods.

k: A senator pushing the Mutant Registration Act
st: Senator Kelly argues that mutants are dangerous and must be registered.
Magneto's machine mutates him, and he dies as his body turns to water.

k: Jean Grey's unleashed, all-powerful dark side
st: Jean returns from Alkali Lake as the Phoenix and destroys Charles Xavier. She sides with Magneto and tears Alcatraz apart in a rage.
Wolverine kills her to stop the destruction.

k: An unstoppable mutant held in a prison convoy
st: Magneto frees Juggernaut from a prison convoy, and he joins the Brotherhood. At Alcatraz he hunts the boy Leech, but Kitty Pryde tricks him into charging headfirst into a wall.

k: A super-fast mutant who can sense other mutants
st: Callisto helps Magneto find mutants and joins his Brotherhood.
Storm kills her in the battle at Alcatraz.

k: A mutant thief who can copy himself
st: Magneto frees Multiple Man from a prison convoy and recruits him.
His copies act as a decoy at the Brotherhood's camp, and soldiers take him in.

k: Logan's savage brother, a mutant soldier
st: Victor fights beside his brother Logan through a century of wars, then joins Stryker's Team X. He hunts down Team X's former members for Stryker and appears to kill Kayla Silverfox. Victor helps Logan defeat Weapon XI, then walks away.

k: Stryker's ultimate weapon, built from Wade Wilson
st: Stryker turns Wade Wilson, a Team X mercenary, into Weapon XI, loaded with stolen mutant powers.
Logan and Victor defeat him, and Logan cuts off his head.
After the credits, his severed head opens its eyes.
In a mid-credits scene, Deadpool travels back in time and shoots Weapon XI dead.

k: Team X's deadly sharpshooter
st: Agent Zero hunts Logan for Stryker and kills the elderly couple who take him in.
Logan downs his helicopter and kills him in the explosion.

k: A venomous mutant doctor serving the Yashida family
st: Posing as Yashida's doctor, Viper plants a parasite in Logan that stops him from healing.
Yukio kills her in the final battle at Yashida's research facility.

k: A dying billionaire Logan saved at Nagasaki
st: Yashida, the soldier Logan saved at Nagasaki, offers to take away Logan's healing power.
He fakes his death and, inside the Silver Samurai armor, starts draining Logan's healing factor.
Mariko stabs him with Logan's claws, and Logan throws him from the tower.

k: Mariko's father and heir to the Yashida empire
st: Shingen sends Yakuza to kidnap his own daughter at her grandfather's funeral.
He duels Logan with a sword and dies on his claws.

k: A ninja archer sworn to protect Mariko
st: Harada's ninjas capture Logan for Yashida's plan.
He turns on Yashida to protect Mariko, and the Silver Samurai kills him.

k: A Nazi scientist who absorbs energy
st: As Klaus Schmidt, a Nazi doctor, he kills young Erik's mother to unlock the boy's powers. Leading the Hellfire Club, he pushes the U.S. and the USSR toward nuclear war over Cuba.
Erik pins him inside his submarine and drives the old coin through his skull.

k: A Hellfire Club telepath who turns to diamond
st: Emma Frost bends a Soviet general's mind to serve Shaw's plan.
Erik captures her in Russia, and the CIA locks her up.
Erik breaks her out, and she joins his Brotherhood.

k: A red-skinned teleporter in the Hellfire Club
st: Azazel teleports into the CIA's base with Shaw and kills the agents there. After Shaw dies, he joins Erik's Brotherhood.
An Azazel variant serves Cassandra Nova in the Void.

k: A Hellfire Club mutant who spins up whirlwinds
st: Riptide fights for Shaw at the CIA base and in the battle off Cuba. After Shaw dies, he joins Erik's Brotherhood.

k: A winged mutant recruited by the CIA
st: Angel abandons the young mutants and joins Shaw after his attack on the CIA base. After Shaw dies, she joins Erik's Brotherhood.

k: Erik Lehnsherr, a Holocaust survivor hunting Nazis
st: Erik hunts the Nazi who killed his mother and teams up with Charles Xavier. He kills Shaw, turns the navies' missiles back on them, and leaves with Mystique as Magneto.
Freed from a Pentagon cell in 1973, he hijacks Sentinels and attacks the White House.
After his family is killed, he becomes a Horseman of Apocalypse and tears at the Earth's metal.
He turns on Apocalypse, then helps rebuild Xavier's school.
Living on Genosha, he hunts Jean for killing Mystique, then fights beside her against the D'Bari.

k: Raven, a shape-shifter raised as Charles's sister
st: Raven embraces her blue form and leaves with Erik as Mystique.
In 1973 she hunts Bolivar Trask, whose experiments have killed mutants she knew. She spares Trask, saves the President from Magneto, and walks away.
She rallies young mutants against Apocalypse and stays to train the X-Men.
An out-of-control Jean Grey throws her onto broken wood, and she dies.

k: A scientist building robots to hunt mutants
st: Trask experiments on captured mutants and sells his Sentinel program in 1973.
After Mystique spares him, he is arrested for selling military secrets.

k: Mutant-hunting robots that rule a dark future
st: In a dark future, Sentinels that copy mutant powers hunt mutants and the humans who help them. In 1973, Magneto hijacks Trask's Sentinel prototypes and attacks the White House.
Mystique spares Trask, and Logan wakes in a future with no Sentinels.

k: A young Army major working with Bolivar Trask
st: Major William Stryker serves as Bolivar Trask's military aide in 1973.
Colonel Stryker raids Xavier's mansion and takes several X-Men to Alkali Lake. Weapon X breaks loose, and his captives escape the base.

k: En Sabah Nur, the first mutant, worshipped as a god
st: Betrayed in ancient Egypt, En Sabah Nur is buried alive for thousands of years.
Woken in 1983, he gathers four Horsemen and seizes Charles Xavier's mind. He sends the world's nuclear missiles into space and starts tearing cities apart.
Jean Grey unleashes the Phoenix and burns him away.

k: A telepathic bodyguard with a blade of energy
st: Psylocke guards the mutant dealer Caliban, then joins Apocalypse as a Horseman. After Apocalypse falls, she flees.

k: A winged mutant cage fighter in East Berlin
st: Apocalypse gives the wounded Angel metal wings and makes him a Horseman.
He dies when the X-Men's jet crashes.

k: Ororo, a Cairo street thief who controls weather
st: Apocalypse makes Ororo his first Horseman and amplifies her powers.
She turns on Apocalypse and joins the X-Men.

k: An X-Man changed by a cosmic force in space
st: Jean absorbs a cosmic force during a space rescue, and her powers grow out of control. She kills Mystique by accident and flees, hunted by the X-Men and Magneto.
She destroys Vuk in space and vanishes in a burst of fiery light.

k: Leader of the D'Bari, shape-shifting aliens
st: Vuk, leader of the shape-shifting D'Bari, manipulates Jean to steal the cosmic force inside her.
Jean takes the power back and destroys Vuk in space.

k: Cyborg security chief for Transigen
st: Pierce and his Reavers hunt Logan to take back Laura, a young mutant.
The children escaped from Transigen turn on him and kill him.

k: Transigen's head scientist
st: Rice runs Transigen's program that breeds mutant children as weapons.

k: A feral clone of Logan in his prime
st: X-24 kills Charles Xavier and the Munson family.
Laura kills him with an adamantium bullet to the head.

k: Francis, who runs a lab that turns people into mutants
st: Ajax tortures Wade Wilson to trigger his mutation, leaving him scarred. He kidnaps Vanessa to lure Wade into a fight.

k: Ajax's super-strong right hand
st: Angel Dust helps Ajax run his lab and fights Colossus at the scrapyard.
Negasonic's blast knocks her out, and Colossus carries her from the wreck.

k: A cybernetic soldier from the future
st: Cable travels back in time to kill Russell before the boy becomes a killer.
He teams up with Deadpool and spends his last time jump saving Wade's life.

k: Russell, an angry young mutant who throws fire
st: Russell attacks the staff of his mutant orphanage and is locked in the Ice Box.
He frees Juggernaut and sets out to kill the orphanage's headmaster.
Moved by Deadpool's sacrifice, he spares the headmaster.

k: Head of a mutant re-education orphanage
st: The headmaster abuses the young mutants in his care.
Dopinder runs him over with his taxi.

k: An unstoppable mutant held in the Ice Box
st: Freed by Russell, Juggernaut tears Deadpool in half and joins the attack on the orphanage.
Colossus, Negasonic and Yukio defeat him at the orphanage.

k: A Juggernaut variant in Cassandra Nova's service
st: In the raid on Cassandra Nova's lair, X-23 kills Juggernaut, and the heroes take his helmet to block her telepathy.

k: A huge mutant in Cassandra Nova's service
st: Blob stands among Cassandra Nova's mutant forces in the Void.

k: The doctor running a hospital for young mutants
st: Dr. Reyes holds five young mutants in a hidden hospital for the Essex Corporation.
She moves to kill Dani Moonstar, and the Demon Bear kills her.

k: A monstrous bear stalking Dani Moonstar
st: The Demon Bear tears into the hospital and the young mutants inside.
Dani faces her fear and calms the bear, which comes from her own power.

k: A mutant master of magnetism fighting for mutantkind
st: Magneto attacks a missile base, and the X-Men stop him.
He builds Asteroid M as a haven for mutants, but his follower Fabian Cortez betrays him.
He joins forces with the X-Men against greater threats, including the Phalanx.
Xavier leaves the X-Men to Magneto, who stands trial for his past crimes.
After the Genosha massacre, he shuts down Earth's magnetic field to force humanity's hand.
As Asteroid M is stopped, he and several X-Men vanish in a flash of light.
Stranded in ancient Egypt, he saves a city from a black hole, and Apocalypse kills him.

k: Giant robots built to hunt mutants
st: Bolivar Trask's Sentinels hunt down mutants, and the X-Men strike back.
Master Mold, the Sentinel factory, turns on its makers and plots to rule humanity.
A giant Wild Sentinel slaughters the mutants of Genosha.
Prime Sentinels, humans fitted with machine parts, hunt mutants around the world.
When Jean puts Bastion's own collar on him, every Prime Sentinel shuts down.

k: The scientist behind the Sentinel program
st: Trask builds the Sentinels to round up mutants.
Rogue hunts Trask for the Genosha attack and lets him fall, and his body rises as a Prime Sentinel until Cable stops it.

k: A geneticist obsessed with mutant DNA
st: Mister Sinister and his Nasty Boys battle the X-Men as he hunts mutant DNA.
He reveals that Madelyne Pryor is his clone of Jean Grey and turns her into the Goblin Queen.
Jean returns as the Phoenix and burns his stolen mutant DNA away, leaving him a powerless old man.

k: Cyclops's wife, who believes she is Jean Grey
st: Learning she is Sinister's clone of Jean, Madelyne becomes the Goblin Queen and attacks the X-Men.
She turns on Sinister and leaves to find her own path.

k: An ancient mutant who preaches survival of the fittest
st: In ancient Egypt, En Sabah Nur embraces his destiny as Apocalypse and kills Magneto.
Apocalypse gathers mutant Horsemen and schemes to rule a world of the strong.
He abducts the world's psychics to remake time, but the X-Men stop him at the Axis of Time.
In the year 3960, he rules the world and wants young Nathan Summers as his next body.
He raises Gambit from the dead as his Horseman, Death, and his mind ends up hiding inside Gambit.
Empowered by the Celestial Eson, Rogue pulls his essence out of Gambit and traps it.

k: Wolverine's savage old enemy
st: Sabretooth stalks Wolverine and clashes with the X-Men again and again.
Xavier tries to reach his better nature, but Sabretooth turns on the X-Men.
He joins Wolverine's raid on a Weapon X lab overrun by the Brood and escapes alive.

k: A shape-shifter who can wear any face
st: Disguised as Gambit, Mystique tries to assassinate Senator Kelly.
In a mid-credits scene, Mystique is shown to have killed Valerie Cooper and taken her place.

k: Cain Marko, Xavier's unstoppable stepbrother
st: Juggernaut smashes his way through the X-Mansion hunting his stepbrother, Charles Xavier.
Working for Erik the Red, he and Black Tom storm Muir Island and carry Lilandra off, until he's thrown into the sea.
He robs banks across the city until Jean makes him forget the X-Men and leave town in peace.

k: A Soviet super soldier with deadly metal coils
st: Revived from cold storage, Omega Red battles Wolverine and the X-Men.
Freed by accident in a Weapon X lab, he attacks Wolverine's team, and Wolverine beats him.

k: A ratings-mad tyrant from another dimension
st: Mojo pulls the X-Men into his dimension to fight for his TV ratings.
He traps Jubilee and Roberto inside a deadly video game.

k: A cosmic force bonded to Jean Grey
st: The Phoenix saves Jean from a shuttle crash in space and bonds with her.
Twisted by Mastermind and the Hellfire Club, it becomes Dark Phoenix and consumes a star.
On the Moon, the Phoenix and Jean part, and Jean survives.
The Phoenix rises in Jean again to stop Bastion and Mister Sinister, then fades away.

k: An illusion-casting member of the Hellfire Club
st: Mastermind uses illusions to pull Jean Grey into the Hellfire Club.

k: Leader of the anti-mutant Friends of Humanity
st: Graydon Creed leads the Friends of Humanity, a hate group that attacks mutants.
Kidnapped by the Acolytes, he is put on trial in the Savage Land until the X-Men get him out.
A news broadcast reports that he has been elected President of the United States.

k: A mutant follower of Magneto on Asteroid M
st: Cortez betrays Magneto and seizes control of Asteroid M.

k: Moira MacTaggert's reality-warping son
st: Proteus escapes Muir Island and bends reality as he hunts for his father.

k: A man with a burning hatred for mutants
st: Bastion is behind the Wild Sentinel that slaughters the mutants of Genosha.
He launches Operation: Zero Tolerance, sending Prime Sentinels after mutants.
Jean shuts down his Sentinels, and he seems to die trying to crash Asteroid M into Earth.

k: A time-traveling pharaoh with advanced weapons
st: Pharaoh Rama-Tut fires a giant beam weapon at En Sabah Nur and the stranded X-Men.
When Apocalypse opens a black hole over his city, he flees to the future in his Sphinx ship.

k: Gambit, raised from the dead as Apocalypse's Horseman
st: Apocalypse raises Gambit from the dead and makes him Death, one of his Horsemen.
As Death, he brainwashes Nightcrawler and kidnaps Rogue.
Rogue pulls Apocalypse out of him, and Gambit comes back to the X-Men.

k: Head of X-Factor, a government team of mutants
st: Valerie Cooper's X-Factor, with Havok and Polaris, hunts X-Force and captures Jubilee.
A mid-credits scene reveals that Mystique has killed the real Valerie Cooper.

k: A powerful mutant among the Acolytes
st: In the Savage Land, Exodus and the Acolytes put the kidnapped Graydon Creed on trial.
The standoff in the Savage Land ends with Exodus dead.

k: Abraham Kieros, a Horseman of Apocalypse
st: Cable's X-Force tracks War down through Caliban, and Archangel executes him.

k: The White Queen of the Hellfire Club's Inner Circle
X-Men: The Animated Series
A telepath working with the government's X-Factor
X-Men '97
st: Emma Frost of the Inner Circle battles Professor X for psychic control of Jean Grey.
Emma Frost tips off X-Force, then leads them into an ambush set by X-Factor.

k: The Danger Room's AI, come to life
st: The Danger Room's AI absorbs Polaris's power, takes an android body as Danger and locks down the mansion.
She hijacks a jet to confront Xavier on Genosha, and Xavier, Jean, Bishop and Polaris defeat her.

k: Insect-like aliens that grow inside living hosts
st: Insect-like Brood aliens try to turn captives into hosts for their young, and the X-Men fight them.
In a Weapon X lab, Dr. Cornelius turns into a Brood alien, and the lab burns the Brood as Wolverine's team escapes.

k: A billionaire and Reed Richards's rival
cl: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
st: Victor Von Doom funds Reed's space mission and is changed by the same cosmic storm.
As his body turns to metal, he takes the name Doom and attacks the Fantastic Four.
Beaten by the Fantastic Four, he freezes solid in his metal form and is shipped to Latveria.
Revived by the Silver Surfer's energy, he steals the Surfer's board and its power.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
Johnny Storm, carrying all four powers, knocks him off the board into the sea.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A cosmic herald who leaves craters across Earth
st: The Silver Surfer streaks around the globe, preparing Earth for his master.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
The U.S. military captures him and holds him in a cell.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
He turns on Galactus and saves Earth.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A vast cosmic cloud that devours worlds
st: Galactus arrives at Earth to consume it.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
The Silver Surfer flies into Galactus and destroys him in a blinding blast.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A U.S. general with a grudge against Reed
st: General Hager forces the Fantastic Four to work with Victor Von Doom to catch the Silver Surfer.
Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer

k: A young vampire who wants to rule humanity
st: Deacon Frost defies the vampire elders and plans to raise the blood god La Magra. He kills the elders and becomes La Magra using Blade's blood.
Blade injects him with anticoagulant darts, and he bursts apart.

k: Frost's mocking vampire lieutenant
st: Quinn serves Frost and survives being burned and maimed by Blade.
Blade finally kills him at the Temple of Eternal Night.

k: Frost's lover and vampire enforcer
st: Mercury helps Frost hunt Blade and raise La Magra.
Blade kills her at the Temple of Eternal Night.

k: A pureblood vampire elder
st: Dragonetti tries to rein Frost in, and Frost leaves him to burn in the sunrise.

k: The first Reaper, a vampire-killing mutant
st: Nomak spreads the Reaper strain, a plague that feeds on vampires. He kills his father, Damaskinos, for creating him.
Beaten by Blade, he drives Blade's sword into himself.

k: An ancient vampire overlord
st: Damaskinos asks Blade for help against the Reapers, hiding that he made them.

k: A brutal Bloodpack vampire who despises Blade
A vampire leader who frames Blade
st: Danica Talos awakens Dracula in the Syrian desert and frames Blade for killing a human.
Blade stabs Drake with the Daystar arrow, and the virus it releases kills her.

k: Danica's brother and fellow vampire leader
st: Asher stands with his sister Danica as her vampires hunt Blade and the Nightstalkers.
Abigail Whistler kills him in the assault on the Talos building.

k: Dracula, the first vampire, woken in the Syrian desert
st: Danica's vampires awaken Drake, the original vampire once known as Dracula.
Blade stabs him with the Daystar arrow, and the virus kills him.

k: A hulking vampire enforcer with metal teeth
st: Grimwood serves Danica as muscle, and Hannibal King kills him in the final assault.

k: A powerful vampire of the House of Chthon
st: Marcus turns Krista Starr into a vampire and makes her his agent. He secretly plots against the pureblood vampires who lead his house. With Blade's help, he unleashes a virus on the purebloods at their conclave, then faces Blade.

k: Wilson Fisk, a businessman secretly running crime
st: The Kingpin hires Bullseye to kill Nikolas Natchios and frame Daredevil.
Daredevil beats him but spares him, and the police arrest him.

k: An Irish assassin who never misses
st: Bullseye kills Nikolas Natchios with Daredevil's own weapon, then kills Elektra.
Daredevil throws him from a church, and he wakes in a guarded hospital bed, his aim still perfect.

k: An ancient order of mystic assassins
st: The Hand sends its deadliest killers to seize Abby Miller, a girl they call the Treasure.

k: The Hand's leading assassin
st: Kirigi leads the Hand's assassins in hunting Elektra and Abby.
Elektra kills him in the hedge maze of her childhood home.

k: A Hand assassin whose touch is poison
st: Typhoid's poisoned kiss nearly kills Elektra.
She dies in the final battle at Elektra's childhood home.

k: A Tampa crime boss and money launderer
st: After his son dies in a sting, Saint has Frank Castle's whole family murdered.
Frank turns Saint against those closest to him, then drags him to his death behind a car.

k: Howard Saint's wife
st: Livia demands that Frank Castle's entire family be killed.
Howard, tricked into believing she is having an affair with Quentin Glass, kills her.

k: Howard Saint's right-hand man
st: Glass runs the Saints' business and helps hunt Frank Castle.
Frank makes Howard believe Glass is sleeping with Livia, and Howard kills him.

k: Howard Saint's surviving son
st: John helps massacre Frank Castle's family, and Frank later kills him.

k: A giant hitman hired by Saint
st: The Russian nearly beats Frank to death in his apartment before Frank kills him.

k: A singing hitman from Memphis
st: Harry Heck hunts Frank for Saint, and Frank kills him in a car shootout.

k: Callisto's gang of outcast mutants
st: Arclight, Psylocke and Quill join Magneto's Brotherhood and storm the cure lab on Alcatraz.
Arclight, Psylocke and Quill are caught in the Phoenix's disintegration wave as the battle on Alcatraz ends.

k: A U.S. Army colonel at the Pentagon
st: Colonel Hendry secretly works for Shaw, until Shaw absorbs a grenade blast and turns it on him.

k: Japan's Minister of Justice, engaged to Mariko
st: Mori admits he conspired with Shingen against Mariko over the company, and Logan throws him out a window.

k: A mutant living on Magneto's Genosha
st: Selene follows Magneto to New York to kill Jean Grey and battles the X-Men.

k: A mutant inmate of the Ice Box
st: Black Tom rides in the prison convoy with Russell and Deadpool, and Cable kills him during his attack.

k: A government agent hunting mutants
st: Henry Peter Gyrich works with Bolivar Trask to round up mutants with the Sentinels.
Hunted by Rogue for his part in the Genosha attack, Gyrich is killed by Bastion.

k: Leader of the Morlocks, mutants living underground
st: Callisto kidnaps Cyclops and Jean for the Morlocks, until Storm beats her in a duel for leadership.

k: Mystique's band of mutant troublemakers
st: Avalanche, Pyro and the Blob back Mystique in her schemes against the X-Men.

k: Sebastian Shaw's secret society of the rich
st: Sebastian Shaw, Donald Pierce and Harry Leland's Inner Circle use Mastermind's illusions to bend Jean Grey to their will.

k: The mad emperor of the Shi'ar
st: Emperor D'Ken hunts for the power of the M'Kraan Crystal and orders the X-Men and the Starjammers killed.
He unleashes the Crystal's power, and the Phoenix traps him inside it.

k: A masked agent of the Shi'ar emperor
st: Erik the Red serves Emperor D'Ken in his hunt for the M'Kraan Crystal.

k: The Shi'ar empire's elite super-powered soldiers
st: Emperor D'Ken sends the Imperial Guard against the X-Men and the Starjammers.

k: A man who turns into a winged reptile
st: In the Savage Land, Sauron battles the X-Men.

k: An armored swordsman in Japan
st: In Japan, the Silver Samurai and his gang terrorize a village, and Wolverine stands against them.

k: A warlord from another world
st: Arkon takes Storm to his world to be his bride, and the X-Men clash with him.

k: A Nazi mastermind in World War II
st: In World War II, the Red Skull clashes with Captain America and Wolverine as they raid a Nazi base to rescue a scientist.

k: A techno-organic hive that absorbs living beings
st: The Phalanx absorbs most of the X-Men, until Beast, Warlock, Forge, Mister Sinister and Magneto destroy it with a virus.

k: A trickster spirit who preys on Storm
st: The Adversary torments a powerless Storm and poisons Forge, until Storm regains her powers and fights it off.

k: A killer with long metal claws
st: Yuriko leads the Reavers against the Morlocks to make Wolverine pay for her father's death, then calls a draw.
Lady Deathstrike joins Wolverine's raid on a Weapon X lab overrun by the Brood, and the team escapes as it explodes.

k: A bloated vampire archivist
st: Blade tortures Pearl with a UV light until he reveals Frost's plan to raise La Magra.

k: A police officer serving the vampires
st: Blade beats information out of Krieger, and Frost kills him for his failure.

k: An elite vampire squad trained to kill Blade
st: Damaskinos's Bloodpack, trained to kill Blade, is forced to hunt the Reapers at his side.
Reapers and sunlight kill the squad one by one, and Nyssa, the last, dies in the sunrise.

k: Damaskinos's human familiar and lawyer
st: Kounen helps Damaskinos hold Blade captive, until Whistler guns him down.

k: A police chief working with the vampires
st: Chief Vreede holds Blade in custody after the vampires frame him for a killing.
At the vampires' blood farm, Blade shoots Vreede for rounding up humans for them.

k: Marcus Van Sciver's vampire enforcer
st: Chase carries out Marcus's schemes and faces Krista in the final showdown.

k: A man acquitted of rape
st: Freed by a jury, Quesada is hunted by Daredevil and dies under a subway train.

k: A towering Hand assassin who shrugs off blows
st: Stone hunts Elektra and Abby for the Hand, and Elektra kills him in the forest.

k: A Hand assassin armed with daggers
st: Kinkou joins the Hand's hunt in the forest, and Abby and Mark kill him with one of his own daggers.

k: Howard Saint's son, buying illegal arms
st: Bobby Saint dies in an FBI arms sting run by undercover agent Frank Castle.

k: A small-time gangster working for the Saints
st: Arrested at the sting, Mickey later becomes Frank's inside man against the Saints.

k: A member of Attilan's Royal Guard
st: Locus joins Auran on Earth to hunt down the royal family for Maximus.
She turns to help Black Bolt and Medusa, then dies of a fatal wound.

k: A gangster tied to Geoffrey Wilder
st: Darius runs crime in Los Angeles until Catherine Wilder shoots him dead.

k: Brigid O'Reilly's violent other half
st: Brigid O'Reilly's dark half splits off as Mayhem and hunts criminals as a lethal vigilante.

k: Pestilence, War, Famine and Death, Apocalypse's backups
st: In the year 3960, Apocalypse's Final Horsemen fall on the time-lost X-Men, until Morph turns the fight as Thor.

k: An Oscorp executive pressuring Dr. Connors
st: Oscorp's Dr. Rajit Ratha orders Connors's serum tested on unwitting veterans, and the Lizard hunts him on a bridge.

k: Oscorp's dying founder, Harry's father
st: Norman Osborn dies of a hereditary illness, and Richard Parker's video reveals Oscorp wanted his research for weapons.

k: A crime boss ruling a Russian prison
st: Kraven gets himself locked in a Russian prison and kills crime boss Semyon Chorney in his private office.

k: Peter Parker, Gwen Stacy's best friend
st: In Gwen's world, Peter Parker turns himself into the Lizard, and he dies after his fight with Spider-Woman.

k: A live-action Prowler from another universe
st: A live-action Prowler from another universe is held in a Spider Society cell with other captured anomalies.

k: Uncle Aaron of Earth-42
st: On Earth-42, Aaron Davis is alive, and he helps his nephew, the Prowler, hold the Miles from Earth-1610 captive.

k: A wax museum artist
st: Parafino, a wax museum artist, traps Spider-Man and Betty Brant above vats of hot wax.

k: A scientist who masters magnetism
st: Snubbed by the Science Hall of Fame, Dr. Matto Magneto seeks revenge and attacks Spider-Man with a magnetic gun.

k: A musician with a sonic instrument
st: The Fiddler uses an instrument that fires destructive sound waves to take revenge on an impresario.

k: A criminal mastermind
st: The Plotter sends his henchmen Cowboy and Ox to steal the blueprints for a missile.

k: The inventor of the Spider-Slayer
st: Henry Smythe builds a Spider-Slayer robot to capture Spider-Man for J. Jonah Jameson.

k: A heavyset mob boss
st: The Kingpin runs a racket that forces druggists to sell fake medicine at gunpoint.
The Kingpin uses a nightclub as the front for a brainwashing scheme.

k: A jewel thief in a giant hat
st: Dr. Dumpty pulls a jewel heist at a gala and is arrested after trapping himself in his own inflated hat.

k: A skeletal being from the fifth dimension
st: Spider-Man comes face to face with the skeletal Infinata, a menace from the fifth dimension.

k: A robotics genius, Alistair's father
st: Norman Osborn hires Spencer Smythe to build Spider-Slayer robots, and Spencer seems to die when the scheme fails.
The Kingpin reveals he has kept Spencer Smythe alive in cryogenic storage all along.

k: Head of the Brand Corporation
st: Herbert Landon offers mutants a cure, but secretly works to build an army of super-mutants for the Kingpin.

k: A Nazi spymaster from World War II
st: The Red Skull teams with the Kingpin to claim a doomsday device hidden since World War II.
He turns his son into Electro, but ends up trapped in another dimension with Captain America.

k: The Red Skull's son
st: The doomsday device turns Kragov, the Red Skull's son and a Moscow police chief, into Electro, later pulled into its vortex.

k: The ruler of a realm on Battleworld
st: On Battleworld, Doctor Doom kidnaps the Thing, then absorbs the Beyonder's power to fight Spider-Man's team.

k: A being formed from ancient symbiotes
st: The Synoptic, a mass of ancient symbiotes, directs Venom and Carnage in their plan to spread symbiotes on Counter-Earth.

k: A rat-like Bestial on Counter-Earth
st: Lady Vermin, a rat-like Bestial on Counter-Earth, clashes with Spider-Man and takes a liking to him.

k: Counter-Earth's version of Kraven
st: The High Evolutionary hires the Hunter to track down and capture Spider-Man.

k: A master thief
st: Master thief Black Cat tries to steal the alien symbiote, then helps Spider-Man stop the Chameleon's crime spree.

k: An arsonist with fire gauntlets
st: Butane burns down a building to make way for a high-rise, and Spider-Man beats him and finds a strange symbol on his gear.

k: A small-time crook with a fiery secret
st: Ben hunts small-time crook Jimmy Addison, who has fire powers, but a rival investigator shoots him and he dies.

k: Twin jewel thieves
st: Two thieves posing as one Human Fly steal jewelry, until Spider-Man tracks them to an abandoned amusement park.
Paroled, twins Stan and Lee Patterson frame Spider-Man for a vault job, but he finds their fly-tracer and catches them.

k: A bookshop owner with a grudge against Jameson
st: Miss Trubble conjures creatures of Greek myth to get revenge on J. Jonah Jameson, until Spider-Man destroys her magic box.

k: A thief who uses illusions and a magic flute
st: The Fakir steals jewels with illusions and charmed crocodiles, until Spider-Man takes his flute and he is arrested.

k: A thief with a shrinking ray
st: The Phantom shrinks loot with a ray and sets robot henchwomen on Spider-Man, who beats them all at his base.

k: A mad scientist who seizes a nuclear reactor
st: The Master Technician lifts Manhattan into the sky with an anti-gravity field and holds it for ransom, until Spider-Man beats him.

k: The Kingpin's son, head of Fisktronics
st: Richard Fisk gives Peter Parker a job, then frames him for selling government secrets with the Chameleon's help.
Spider-Man and Daredevil clear Peter's name, and Richard is convicted and sent to prison.
From prison, he and Tombstone frame Robbie Robertson, until Spider-Man and Jameson prove Robbie innocent.

k: A scientist whose cloning work was banned
st: Miles Warren clones Hydro-Man and Mary Jane in an underwater lab, and when both dissolve he eyes a scrap of Spider-Man's suit.

k: Leader of the mercenary Wild Pack
st: In Moscow, Silver Sable's Wild Pack seize an informant and leave Spider-Man and Robertson with a ticking bomb.
She captures Spider-Man, the Kingpin and the Insidious Six, then teams up with Spider-Man against the Red Skull.

k: An imprisoned burglar, Black Cat's father
st: During the Vault breakout, inmate Walter Hardy helps Spider-Man and is revealed as the burglar who killed Ben Parker.
Ashamed of his crime, he chooses to stay in prison instead of escaping with his daughter.

k: Kraven the Hunter's partner
st: Calypso Ezili, Kraven the Hunter's partner and lover, is at his side when he comes to New York to hunt Spider-Man.

k: An aide to the pharaoh Rama-Tut
st: In ancient Egypt, Candra serves the pharaoh Rama-Tut, who abandons her when he flees in his time machine.
Now the immortal X-Ternal, she is summoned by Gambit, who kills her and gives her power to Rogue.

k: A huge mutant cage fighter
st: The Blob loses a cage fight to Angel in an underground mutant fight club in East Berlin.

k: A Genosha mutant who fights with his braids
st: Ariki follows Magneto to New York to kill Jean Grey and battles the X-Men.

k: A smooth agent who signs up the dying
st: The Recruiter offers the dying Wade Wilson a secret cure, luring him into Ajax's program.
Hunted down by Deadpool, he gives up Ajax's whereabouts, and Deadpool kills him.

k: Juggernaut's partner, Banshee's cousin
st: Hired by Erik the Red, Black Tom and Juggernaut attack Muir Island and carry Lilandra off to Cassidy Keep.
As Gladiator of the Imperial Guard routs the X-Men, Black Tom escapes with Erik the Red.

k: A winged warrior allied with Apocalypse
st: Deathbird and Apocalypse rescue Fabian Cortez from the falling Asteroid M.

k: A seductive vampire
st: Racquel lures a young man to a vampire blood rave, which Blade then raids.

k: A psychiatrist examining Blade in custody
st: Dr. Edgar Vance, a psychiatrist secretly serving the vampires, declares Blade psychotic so he can be handed over to them.

k: A child-like pureblood elder of the House of Chthon
st: Charlotte, an elder of the House of Chthon, comes to America to check on Marcus's Aurora Project. After a plane crash, she and her servant Thorne slaughter a small town for the blood to heal.

k: A Hand assassin whose tattoos come to life
st: Tattoo joins Kirigi's assassins hunting Elektra, Abby and Mark for the Hand.
He sends snakes to seize Abby in a hedge maze, and Elektra snaps his neck.

k: The Kingpin's personal aide
st: Wesley Owen Welch works as the Kingpin's aide, screening visitors and pushing for tighter security as Daredevil closes in.

k: Howard Saint's Cuban business partners
st: Joe and Mike Toro warn Howard Saint they will take their money elsewhere as Castle destroys their laundered cash.

k: Lt. Flores's corrupt partner
st: Anthony Wall, known as AWOL, attacks Livvie's family on Catherine Wilder's orders.
As PRIDE's main agent, he kills Flores and kidnaps Livvie to find the Runaways.
Trapped at the Runaways' hostel, he and his men vanish when Nico unleashes a new power.

k: A street kid with super strength
st: Topher joins the Runaways, hiding that his strength comes from the rocks he is addicted to.
Exposed as a liar at his parents' house, he lashes out in a rage and is crushed by a dumpster he threw.
